content:
Apple TV is rolling out a slew of announcements at San Diego Comic-Con this weekend, headlining its main stage in Hall H. Kicking things off is its new sci-fi epic "Neuromancer" (adapted from William Gibson's groundbreaking novel of the same name), which has finally locked in its premiere date: January 22.

The streaming service also dropped new trailers for Season 2 of "Dark Matter" and the upcoming film "Matchbox," which you can check out via the links below...

This gritty cyberpunk series "Neuromancer" stars Callum Turner as hacker Case, who teams up with a killer named Molly to take on a corporate dynasty.

The first trailer for the series has now been released, but fans of the franchise will need to wait patiently. "Neuromancer" will premiere on January 22, 2027; the first season will have ten episodes.

Also unveiled today was the official trailer for Season 2 of "Dark Matter," which is set to air at the end of August.

The first season of "Dark Matter" aired in 2024, adapted from the novel of the same name by author Blake Crouch. Season 2 will go beyond the original story, but all scripts are still written by Crouch himself. It seems the many clones of Jason around the world have yet to be eliminated.

Finally, Apple also released a trailer for the upcoming film "Matchbox," starring John Cena.

"Matchbox" is adapted from a toy car brand, and the plot appears to be a typical CIA agent and conspiracy theory-style storyline. It has all the hallmarks of car chases, helicopters, and classic action comedy elements. Audiences can watch "Matchbox" on the streaming platform in October.

Apple's lineup at this year's Comic-Con also includes live panel discussions for shows like "Widows Bay" and "Silo." This marks the company's largest participation in this annual event, securing a 2-hour slot in Hall H for the first time.
